title: Genetically wild-type planarian cells can store more than one target morphology

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Genetically wild-type planarian cells can store more than one target morphology

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In planaria, a brief (2-day) physiological intervention can reset the bioelectric circuit that controls head number from the default one-head pattern memory to a two-head pattern, so the same genetically wild-type cells can harbour multiple bioelectrically encoded target morphologies that guide regeneration.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: In this case, the exact same hardware (genetically wild-type planarian cells) can harbor multiple representations of the bioelectrically encoded target morphology that guides the cellular collectives during regeneration [193–195].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Bioelectric networks as reprogrammable interface to morphogenetic capabilities”. Scope: Planarians (Dugesia japonica and related species) during regeneration

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-12: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.71

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head number, treatment history, and voltage are measurable, and repeated regeneration provides a strong persistence test. Existing data can establish the phenotype but may not fully exclude non-bioelectric inherited states.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Verify genotype identity, transient treatment, bioelectric state, and head number over repeated untreated regeneration rounds. Persistent one- versus two-head outcomes in genetically matched animals, reversible by voltage reset, support multiple stable physiological target states.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Wild type does not guarantee complete genetic identity.

Raw multi-round lineage records may not be deposited.

Persistent biochemical or microbial changes could rival bioelectric storage.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The memory operationalization is the right kind: a persistent change in regenerative outcome after a transient stimulus, with a reset. Published planarian experiments report that pattern for wild-type stocks. Those counts are not a reusable dataset, and several non-bioelectric stores fit the same persistence, so existing reports test the phenomenon only in part.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Treat memory as a regenerative head number that stays altered after a brief physiological treatment is washed out, in animals whose genotype is the wild-type stock, and that can be reset by a later physiological treatment. Stable two-headed regeneration after a two-day treatment, reversible without a genetic change, would support multiple stored targets; immediate reversion after washout, or a mutation that co-segregates with head number, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Head-number counts are in the experimental papers, not in a public individual-level file, and the lines have not been shown by a deposited genome to be free of mutations.

Persistent drug, epigenetic marks, or microbiome changes can store the phenotype without a bioelectric target representation.
